evidence.summary: BLACKBOX score can be closely reconstructed as a continuous target from age, baseline_score, comorbidity_ratio, dependants, prior_visits, recent_admissions, requested_beds, vitals_index, ward, and years_registered. The score itself was excluded from model inputs to prevent target leakage.
Five-fold out-of-fold evaluation achieved RMSE 0.105696, MAE 0.057992, and R2 0.832649, indicating strong reconstruction of the continuous BLACKBOX scoring behavior.
Optimizing the score-to-decision boundary produced a threshold of 0.590. This threshold achieved 90.70% decision accuracy and 94.50% balanced accuracy on the out-of-fold predictions.
The observed data contains 109 APPROVE cases and 20 DECLINE cases. Balanced regression weighting was therefore used so the minority DECLINE behavior was not overwhelmed by the majority APPROVE class.

At the optimized threshold, all 20 observed DECLINE cases were identified, producing 20 true DECLINE predictions and 0 false APPROVE predictions. There were 97 true APPROVE and 12 false DECLINE predictions.
On the known champion validation case, BLACKBOX returned score 0.9793 and APPROVE. The reconstructed model returned score 0.9793 and APPROVE, with an absolute score difference of 0.000000.

The final reconstruction uses ExtraTreesRegressor with 1200 trees, max_features=0.8, max_depth=None, and min_samples_leaf=1, providing a flexible nonlinear approximation of the observed scoring behavior.
